findings.title: retryCount increment is a read-modify-write race, not atomic
findings.body: Both the `else` branch (line 184) and the `catch` block (line 195) compute `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched earlier in `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap (this endpoint is triggered by an external cron and processing a large batch can exceed the cron interval), both runs read the same retryCount and write the same value, losing an increment. More importantly, if the row was already updated by a concurrent run, the stale value overwrites it. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` so concurrent runs cannot clobber each other's counts.

findings.title: retryCount update in catch block can throw and abort the entire cron run
findings.body: The `catch` block performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update`. If the original error was a database connectivity failure (a plausible cause of scheduling errors), this update will also fail, and since nothing catches it the exception propagates out of the `for` loop, aborting processing of all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch and returning a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or use updateMany which won't throw on a missing row) so one failing reminder doesn't kill the whole run.

findings.title: Retry-based deletion silently drops reminders that failed for transient reasons
findings.body: The `deleteMany` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` deletes any reminder that failed scheduling twice, regardless of why. Failures counted include transient infrastructure problems (Twilio outage, DB errors thrown inside the try, e.g. the `prisma.profile.findFirst` lookup) since the catch block increments retryCount for any error, not just SMS provider rejections like invalid phone numbers. After two transient failures the reminder is permanently deleted and the attendee/host never receives the SMS, with no notification or logging of the deletion. Consider only incrementing for known-permanent provider errors, or at least logging deleted reminder IDs.
